title: TVS Motor Signals Potential Spin-Off of TVS Credit Financial Services Arm
excerpt: Chairman Sudarshan Venu told shareholders the company will evaluate alternatives for its financial services subsidiary TVS Credit, which now has a ₹30,000-crore asset base and 24.4 million customers.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • TVS Motor may spin off its financial services arm, TVS Credit, to enhance shareholder value.
  • TVS Credit's asset base exceeds ₹30,000 crore, serving 24.4 million customers with 26% growth in FY26.
  • TVS Motor achieved record sales of 5.89 million vehicles and revenue of ₹47,270 crore in FY26.
  • The company is expanding into Europe and investing in electric vehicles and AI technologies.
  • TVS Motor's international operations contribute over 25% of total revenue, targeting growth in Africa and Latin America.

TVS Motor Company Chairman and Managing Director Sudarshan Venu has signalled that the automaker may spin off its financial services subsidiary TVS Credit Services, marking the first time the Chennai-based conglomerate has publicly considered unlocking value from the fast-growing NBFC.

"The company may, at an appropriate time, in stages, guided by long-term strategic considerations, evaluate alternatives, including a possible separation of the financial services business, to further strengthen and unlock shareholder value," Venu told shareholders at the company's Annual General Meeting on Wednesday.

TVS Credit: From Financing Arm to Standalone Powerhouse

What began as a captive financing arm for two-wheeler buyers has grown into a substantial standalone business. TVS Credit, rated AA+ by all three major Indian rating agencies, reported disbursement growth of 26% in FY26 and ended the year with an asset base exceeding ₹30,000 crore, according to PTI. The subsidiary now serves over 24.4 million customers across two-wheelers, consumer durables, tractors, and other products.

In Q1 FY27, TVS Credit posted total income of ₹1,918 crore — a 13% year-on-year increase — and net profit of ₹208 crore, up 15% from the same period last year, according to The Hindu BusinessLine. The company disbursed loans to over 14 lakh new customers during the quarter, bringing its total customer base to nearly 2.6 crore.

> **"TVS Credit, rated AA+ by all three major Indian rating agencies, reported disbursement growth of 26% in FY26 and ended the year with an asset base exceeding ₹30,000 crore, according to PTI."**

"TVS Credit, rated AA+ by all three major Indian rating agencies, reported disbursement growth of 26% in FY26 and ended the year with an asset base exceeding ₹30,000 crore, according to PTI."

"Rated AA+ by all three major rating agencies, TVS Credit is continuing to grow with prudence, with purpose, and with the same values of TVS."

— Sudarshan Venu, Chairman and MD, TVS Motor Company

TVS Motor holds an 80.76% stake in TVS Credit on a fully diluted basis, having invested ₹172 crore in additional capital as recently as November 2025 to improve the subsidiary's capital adequacy ratio.

Record Year Fuels Confidence

The spin-off consideration comes on the back of TVS Motor's strongest-ever financial year. The company reported record annual sales of 5.89 million vehicles in FY26, with revenue hitting ₹47,270 crore and EBITDA reaching ₹6,079 crore, according to Fortune India.

International operations now contribute more than a quarter of overall revenue, with volumes crossing 1.59 million units across over 90 countries. Venu said the company is entering the European market while viewing Africa, Latin America, and Asia as long-term strategic growth paths.

"Africa, in particular, sits at an extraordinary inflection point. A young population with mobility needs that will only grow. We are a trusted brand in the African market, and we very much intend to build on that," Venu said.

Electric Vehicles and AI Push

TVS Motor sold over 3.71 lakh electric two-wheelers in FY26, a 33% year-on-year increase driven by its expanded TVS iQube portfolio and the newly launched Orbiter scooter. The company has established more than 1,000 EV dealerships and supported 5,000 public charging points across India, according to Fortune India.

Research and development spending exceeded ₹1,250 crore during the year, with over 2,000 engineers working on connected technologies, electrification, and next-generation mobility solutions. Venu also highlighted investments in generative AI and a new design and engineering hub in Bologna, Italy, through Engines Engineering.

Financial Services Strategy Extends Beyond TVS Credit

When a shareholder asked about TVS Motor's investment in Jana Small Finance Bank, Venu connected it to the company's broader financial services vision. "Our investment in Jana is part of this vision of financial services of an aspirational India, and we see lot of synergies and we believe that the bank will do well," he said, according to The Hindu BusinessLine.

Premium motorcycles are also strengthening the portfolio. The Apache RTX 300 and NTORQ 150 have bolstered the company's premium lineup, while the revived Norton brand is slated for launches across the UK, Europe, India, and the US during the current fiscal year.

What's Next

Venu offered no timeline for a potential TVS Credit separation, saying only that it would happen "at an appropriate time" and "in stages." For investors in the Indian auto and financial services space, the move could create significant value — spinning off a high-growth NBFC with a ₹30,000 crore asset base would follow a pattern seen across Indian conglomerates seeking to simplify structures and attract specialized investors. TVS Motor's overall international business, Venu added, is expected to demonstrate resilience and continued growth in FY26-27.
